svg.title: Judgment Lien Survival Path on Real Property
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-judgment-lien-survival-funnel; chapter number: 6; chart type: funnel; title: Judgment Lien Survival Path on Real Property; subtitle: Abstract, recording, interest, revival, and bankruptcy checkpoints; caption: A money judgment becomes a lien on land only once abstracts are issued and recorded, then must accrue, be revived on time, and clear the bankruptcy lookback to keep its place in line.; assumptions note: Each stage value is the figure the cited practitioner stated for that step, in its own unit (originals, counties, percent, years, days); widths are not conversion counts.; note: Sources - Bobby Benjy (hJmfkC9gu4c), David Babel (q6PjSqG-sF4), Five Minute Legal Master Series (V5NrY_biljg).; stages: label: Abstract Issued by the Clerk; value: 3; display: 3 sealed originals; conversion: One original per target county; detail: In Bobby Benjy's worked example the LA County Superior Court clerk issued 3 sealed abstracts from the one-page California form.; label: Recorded in Each Target County; value: 3; display: 3 counties; conversion: Orange, San Francisco, and Contra Costa through an attorney service; detail: Benjy records in major counties plus every county where research shows the debtor owns land; a recorded abstract attaches when the debtor buys later.; label: Lien Accrues Interest Until Payoff; value: 9; display: 9 percent per year; conversion: Payoff required before sale or refinance; detail: David Babel describes a Bronx Supreme Court judgment lien accruing 9 percent a year that must be paid off even after a Chapter 7 discharge.; label: Revival Filed Inside the Window; value: 5; display: 5 years from entry of judgment; conversion: Late revival survives but goes to the end of the line; detail: Five Minute Legal Master Series sets the Pennsylvania revival deadline that keeps lien priority against intervening liens.; label: Bankruptcy Lookback Cleared; value: 90; display: 90 days before the bankruptcy filing; conversion: Liens filed inside the window can be avoided; detail: Babel says a judgment lien filed within 90 days of filing can be avoided on a primary residence and on investment properties.

text.title: Judgment Lien Survival Path on Real Property
text.tspan: Judgment Lien Survival Path on Real Property

circle.title: label: Abstract Issued by the Clerk; value: 3; display: 3 sealed originals; conversion: One original per target county; detail: In Bobby Benjy's worked example the LA County Superior Court clerk issued 3 sealed abstracts from the one-page California form.

label: Recorded in Each Target County; value: 3; display: 3 counties; conversion: Orange, San Francisco, and Contra Costa through an attorney service; detail: Benjy records in major counties plus every county where research shows the debtor owns land; a recorded abstract attaches when the debtor buys later.

label: Lien Accrues Interest Until Payoff; value: 9; display: 9 percent per year; conversion: Payoff required before sale or refinance; detail: David Babel describes a Bronx Supreme Court judgment lien accruing 9 percent a year that must be paid off even after a Chapter 7 discharge.

label: Revival Filed Inside the Window; value: 5; display: 5 years from entry of judgment; conversion: Late revival survives but goes to the end of the line; detail: Five Minute Legal Master Series sets the Pennsylvania revival deadline that keeps lien priority against intervening liens.

label: Bankruptcy Lookback Cleared; value: 90; display: 90 days before the bankruptcy filing; conversion: Liens filed inside the window can be avoided; detail: Babel says a judgment lien filed within 90 days of filing can be avoided on a primary residence and on investment properties.

text.title: Assumptions: Each stage value is the figure the cited practitioner stated for that step, in its own unit (originals, counties, percent, years, days); widths are not conversion counts.
